items.title: Do Language Models Know Who Fails? Look-Ahead Bias in LLM Credit-Risk Assessment
items.claim: LLM credit prediction beats baselines only because models memorized bankruptcy outcomes in training data.

items.title: When Financial Fine-tuning Fails: A Three-Level Detectability Analysis of Numerical Hallucination in Domain-Adapted Language Models
items.claim: Financial domain fine-tuning increases LLM hallucination from 5% to 98% despite numeracy supervision.

items.title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
items.claim: More capable LLM traders exhibit correlated behavior that concentrates rather than diversifies market risk.

items.title: Convex Modeling of Price Cross-Impact over Time
items.claim: Models omitting cross-impact and transient decay systematically overestimate costs for relative-value trades.
